unit_label: BRBL::MOD_C::U15: Handle third-party recovery notices, joint funds and discharge safeguards

payload.title: A third-party notice requires an ownership and obligation check
payload.core_explanation_md:
The described section 28 route can require a third party holding or owing the debtor money to pay the Recovery Officer. The notice does not make every rupee at that institution the debtor property. The applicable exemptions, joint-holder notices and rebuttable share presumption matter. A person genuinely not holding or owing the stated amount has the described sworn-objection route.

Payment in compliance with the notice receives the stated receipt and discharge to that extent. False objections and noncompliance have their own consequences, but they should not be assumed without applying the conditions. Section29 borrows specified tax-recovery procedures with necessary modifications; this does not turn the underlying bank debt into a newly assessed income tax.

self_check.prompt_text: Does a notice targeting one joint holder automatically establish that all joint funds belong to that debtor?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Apply the share evidence, presumption and safeguards.

payload.stem_md: A notice concerns one debtor in a joint fund. Evidence shows another holder owns a separate share. What must the responding institution examine?

options.text_md: The ownership evidence, applicable presumption, notice scope and exemptions
options.explanation_md: A notice does not make third-party property the debtor own money.

options.text_md: Only the largest account balance at the institution
options.explanation_md: An unrelated balance is not the legal target.

options.text_md: Whether the debtor name appears first on the form
options.explanation_md: Name order alone does not resolve beneficial shares.

options.text_md: A rule that all joint money always belongs to one debtor
options.explanation_md: The source describes a rebuttable share framework.

payload.correct_explanation_md: A notice does not make third-party property the debtor own money.

payload.stem_md: A third party makes the legally required payment to the Recovery Officer under the notice. What corresponding record matters?

options.text_md: A second automatic liability for the same amount to the debtor
options.explanation_md: The described compliant payment carries discharge to that extent.

options.text_md: A receipt stating that all unrelated debts are also paid
options.explanation_md: Discharge must match the actual obligation and amount.

options.text_md: The payment receipt and extent of statutory discharge
options.explanation_md: The record protects against treating the same paid amount as still owed to the debtor.

options.text_md: A new tax assessment replacing the bank claim
options.explanation_md: Borrowed recovery procedures do not change the nature of the underlying debt.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The record protects against treating the same paid amount as still owed to the debtor.
